entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts in the family, both about the ordinary descendant Virasoro constraints. (a) “Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization” (dated October 5, 2026) proves a transfer theorem, its main theorem (thm:main). For a smooth connected complex projective variety B and an arbitrary algebraic vector bundle E of rank r ≥ 2, with X = P_B(E) the lines in the fibres, it claims V(B) ⇒ V(X). Here V(Y) means L_k^Y Z_Y = 0 for all k ≥ −1, where Z_Y is the total ordinary descendant potential with full cohomology and integral curve classes, the L_k are Getzler/Katz first-Hodge operators, and the zero-mode constant is C_Y = χ(Y)/16 − str(μ_Y²)/4. The method: an auxiliary space W = P_B(E ⊕ O); localization factoring its ancestor potential through the two fixed theories B and X; a genus-zero shift operator whose spectral branches are λ + h with h^r(h + λ) = y, one branch tending to 0 (B) and r tending to λ (X); quantization of the block modes; continuation between branches by monodromy of the covering h ↦ h^r(h + λ); and fixing the scalar in L_0 by the commutators [L_{-1}, L_1] = −2L_0 and [L_0, L_k] = −kL_k. The manuscript says this covers every genus, each integral curve class and all insertions, including primitive and odd classes, and applies to towers of projective bundles. (b) “Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections” (dated September 24, 2026) claims the unconditional statement (main theorem, thm:main, in its introduction): for every smooth complete intersection X in projective space P^N over C, the ordinary unreduced total descendant potential satisfies L_k^X Z_X = 0 for k ≥ −1, in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from H*(X; C), including primitive and odd classes and with no semisimplicity hypothesis. The method: induction on dimension and then on the complexity Σ(d_i − 1) of the defining degrees, using a degeneration X ⇝ U ∪_D Bl_S M; a tested transport theorem (sew:transport) that carries scalar tests of the Virasoro error through capped chains of ruled pieces; a primitive detector (det:detection) built from a Hodge–Riemann positive form, so that vanishing of the scalar tests forces vanishing of the error on primitive inputs; toric-bundle transfer (ind:toric), taken from Coates–Givental–Tseng, for the projective-bundle pieces; and a deformation argument (ind:deformation) from very general to all smooth members.
entries.delivers: (a) A conditional transfer and nothing more. If V holds for a smooth connected projective base B, it holds for P_B(E) for every algebraic bundle E of rank ≥ 2, with no splitting or positivity hypothesis, and so for towers of such bundles over any base that satisfies V. The manuscript itself draws two consequences, both resting on cited results: with Okounkov–Pandharipande’s theorem for smooth target curves, V for projective bundles over smooth projective curves and their towers; and, per its introduction, the conclusion for bases with generically semisimple quantum cohomology, which the introduction attributes to Iritani–Koto combined with Givental–Teleman. Its statement of V is the first-Hodge, super, unreduced form with the stated constant, which matches the list’s “half of the Virasoro algebra” formulation. Read with (b), which supplies V for complete intersection bases, (a) would give V for projective bundles over those bases and their towers. That combination is my inference; neither manuscript states it, and (a) does not cite (b). (b) An unconditional proof, but only for one class: smooth complete intersections in P^N, in all genera, all curve classes and with arbitrary insertions including primitive and odd ones. The manuscript says this “resolves the Virasoro conjecture positively for projective-space complete intersections”. Its introduction lists partial earlier results (genus zero by Liu–Tian and Dubrovin–Zhang; Calabi–Yau with H¹ = 0 by Getzler; target curves by Okounkov–Pandharipande; semisimple targets by Givental and Teleman; genus one for Fano complete intersections by Guo–Zhang–Zhou) and says the present argument covers all genera and insertions at once. The list’s statement concerns every smooth projective variety; (b) does not reach beyond projective complete intersections.
entries.remains: (a) Nothing unconditional: V for the base is the entire input, and the manuscript supplies no base case of its own. If the base is not already known to satisfy V, the conjecture is untouched. For the list’s wording, every smooth projective variety that is not a projective bundle over a base known to satisfy V is outside (a). (b) Every smooth projective variety that is not a complete intersection in projective space, including complete intersections in other ambient spaces and all varieties that are not complete intersections. The list’s “every smooth projective variety” is therefore open beyond the class (b) treats.
entries.direction: (a) reduces the conjecture for projective bundles to the conjecture for the base (conditional transfer). (b) proves the conjecture for one class: smooth complete intersections in projective space.
entries.conditional_on: (a) The hypothesis V(B) on the base is the theorem’s only assumption. The proof relies on cited results used with their stated hypotheses: Iritani’s equivariant shift-operator theorem (the text asserts W meets its semiprojectivity and weight hypotheses, and that its seminegativity condition is automatic for a complete target); the Coates–Givental quantum Riemann–Roch theorem; Givental’s quantization formalism; Getzler’s super conventions; and Coates–Givental–Tseng’s ancestor localization, which the text adapts and extends to a positive-dimensional orbit family. The introduction’s semisimple and curve consequences rely on Iritani–Koto, Givental–Teleman and Okounkov–Pandharipande respectively. The manuscript does not depend on (b). (b) The theorem assumes nothing beyond the smoothness and projectivity of X. It depends on published inputs used with their stated hypotheses: the Coates–Givental–Tseng toric-bundle theorem (Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.3 of that paper) for projective-bundle pieces; Hu–Li–Ruan’s nonzero projective-space fibre invariants; Abramovich–Fantechi relative theory and configuration spaces (AF2016, AFConfigurations) with the Abramovich–Marcus–Wise comparison; Maulik–Pandharipande’s relative reconstruction; Steenbrink’s limiting mixed Hodge structures and Fujisawa’s ordered model; the Argüz–Bousseau–Pandharipande–Zvonkine splitting geometry and complete-intersection Noether–Lefschetz statement (ABPZ §5.2); Witten–Kontsevich for zero-dimensional targets; and Getzler’s 1999 convention with the Hori-type L_0 equation for the scalar. It does not depend on (a).
entries.doubts: (a) The theorem is conditional, and the semisimple and curve consequences are stated in the introduction as following from cited results rather than proved in the paper. The two manuscripts disagree on what Okounkov–Pandharipande proved: (a) says it proves the constraints for smooth target curves including odd insertions, while (b) describes the same theorem (OP2003, Theorem 3) as fixed-degree relative constraints for target curves. The curve-base consequence in (a) depends on which description is right, and (a) does not address the difference. The scalar normalization (Lemma cont:commutators) is argued in compressed form: the normal-order constant −½ str(1/4 − μ_Y²) is asserted, the parity sign is checked on two Darboux summands, and the general computation is referred to Givental’s Section 2. Several arguments are signposted forward, for example “the continuation argument will establish its separate finiteness assertion”, and the quantized operators are defined by formal exponential series in a Novikov completion, with the finiteness described rather than fully written out. (b) The argument is long and in several places compressed, with steps justified by “the same argument applies” or “proves directly”. Examples: the coherent single-class lifts of exceptional generators in Lemma ind:blowup-data (justified “as can be seen from” the strict transform of E × A¹); the claim in Lemma ind:degrees that the local monodromy on exceptional surfaces is the identity; and the local constancy of the Hermitian-square test in Lemma ind:deformation, which relies on a Hodge-balance argument written briefly. The source exposition of the product comparison (Abramovich–Fantechi §4.7.1) is stated to assume that each connected component carries a marking or relative root “expressly for simplicity”. The manuscript asserts that its proof extends to unmarked stable components, but does not write that extension in full, and the cohomological evaluation step depends on it (evaluation.tex, Proposition on group products). The tested transport theorem is restricted to admissible singles (algebraic classes, or classes from fixed projective sources through algebraic correspondences). The text explicitly does not assert transport for arbitrary flat Hodge correspondences, so the primitive part is recovered only through the positivity detector on the target itself. The toric-bundle scalar step for k = 0 relies on the first-Hodge L_0 equation with the constant C_Y being the usual Hori equation, which is cited to Getzler rather than reproved. The curve-class statement is first proved on very general fibres and then extended by deformation invariance, and the degree separation depends on Noether–Lefschetz exclusions for surfaces. The positivity argument (det:norm) identifies the conjugate coefficient on a second ordinary replica in a few sentences.
